rationale: This recombines exactly the three ingredients of the archive's "Accrual-Financed Capex Strain" (capex, weak operating cash flow, total accruals) with a MIN/industry-rank wrapper instead of a product, making it a structural re-expression rather than a new mechanism.

The earnings-quality story is coherent and not a direct archive repeat, but dp/ppent is mechanically depressed by recent PPE additions (new assets inflate the denominator before depreciation catches up), so the interaction is largely a convex restatement of PPE growth itself rather than an independent conditioning variable.

Two problems: it is a one-leg swap on the archive's "Accrual-Financed Capex Strain" (recch replacing total accruals inside the identical capex × SUMRANK structure), and the sign is inverted because Compustat recch is a cash-flow item that is negative when receivables rise, so high RANK(recch/at) means receivables are falling, contradicting the stated hypothesis.

Same sign inconsistency — invch is the cash-flow "decrease (increase) in inventory" item, so industry-high invch/at identifies inventory liquidation, not the hypothesized buildup — and even corrected the construction is just a conditional intersection of two well-documented standalone anomalies (inventory growth and capex/investment).

The debt-issuance leg is a genuinely new economic channel relative to the archive's capex–accrual–cash-flow signals and the sign direction is internally consistent, but a triple product of [0,1] ranks concentrates identification in the all-high corner and stacks three separately published anomalies, so any alpha will be hard to attribute to the interaction itself.

This is an explicitly cosmetic respecification of the archive's failed "Accrual Upshift Capex Downshift" (TREND+WINSOR substituted for ACCEL on identical inputs), and that signal's FMB slope came in with the wrong sign, so smoothing addresses noise rather than the diagnosed economic failure.
